issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Notifications: breakfast, hydration & weekly weigh-in push reminders are SILENTLY suppressed for (almost) every user by send-time optimization.

ROOT CAUSE (backend). app/services/notification_jobs.py sends these reminders with notification_type 'breakfast_reminder' (8:00 AM IST), 'water_reminder' (3:00 PM IST), 'weight_reminder' (Mon 8:00 AM IST), 'dinner_reminder' (7:30 PM IST) — all trigger_source='scheduled'. In notification_service.py send_notification() Check 7 calls should_defer_scheduled_notification() -> get_optimal_send_time(type). But SEND_TIME_DEFAULTS (notification_service.py:139) has NO entry for breakfast_reminder / dinner_reminder / water_reminder / weight_reminder — only 'meal_reminder' (12), 'diet_reminder' (12), 'workout_reminder' (7), 'streak_*' (20), 'general' (18). So for any user with <7 notification-open events in the last 30 days (_MIN_DATA_POINTS=7 -> the majority of users, and EVERY new user) the "optimal hour" falls back to SEND_TIME_DEFAULTS['general'] = 18:00 for all four types.

should_defer then defers whenever |current_hour - 18| > 1 (and not the 0/23 wrap). Python-verified against the actual constants:
  breakfast_reminder runs@ 8 IST  default_optimal=18  DEFERRED(suppressed)=True
  water_reminder     runs@15 IST  default_optimal=18  DEFERRED(suppressed)=True
  weight_reminder    runs@ 8 IST  default_optimal=18  DEFERRED(suppressed)=True
  dinner_reminder    runs@19 IST  default_optimal=18  DEFERRED(suppressed)=False   (survives by luck, 19~=18)

WORSE: "deferral" has NO reschedule. should_defer_scheduled_notification's docstring says "the caller should skip sending now and reschedule", but the ONLY consumer (send_notification.py:326-331) just sets suppressed=True + suppression_reason='send_time_deferred_to_18h'. grep confirms no reschedule/re-enqueue anywhere. The jobs run ONCE per day at a fixed cron (backend.py:16098-16121) and never re-fire. So the deferred reminder is dropped for the day: create_notification still runs with send_push=False (an in-app inbox row appears) but NO push is ever delivered.

EXPECTED: the daily 8:00 AM breakfast push fires at 8:00 AM. ACTUAL: suppressed, "deferred to 18h" — 18:00 never comes back around for that job.

REPRO: user with fcm_token, active plan, last_active within 14d, hasn't logged breakfast, sparse/zero notification opens -> breakfast_reminder job (2:30 UTC) -> send_notification returns {sent:false, reason:'send_time_deferred_to_18h'}. Identical for hydration (9:30 UTC) and Monday weigh-in.

COMPOUNDING (note, not the core bug): weekly_scheduled_cap defaults to 3 (db_models.py:322) and the max the FE offers is 5/week — less than the 7+/week daily cadence — so even the reminders that clear send-time defer get throttled to 'frequency_cap' after 3 sends in a rolling 7-day window.

FIX (pick one): (1) add breakfast_reminder/dinner_reminder/water_reminder/weight_reminder to SEND_TIME_DEFAULTS at their true fixed hours (8/19/15/8) so should_defer never fires against a reminder's own scheduled time; (2) skip send-time optimization entirely for fixed-time reminder types (apply it only to genuinely time-flexible types); or (3) actually implement the reschedule the docstring promises. Files: app/services/notification_service.py:139-243, app/services/notification_jobs.py:90-221, backend.py:16098-16121.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Notifications: "Plan ending soon" reminders never fire again for a returning user on a 2nd/3rd plan — the dedup is all-time + per-user, not per-plan.

BACKEND. app/services/notification_jobs.py plan_ending_soon() (~L228). For each threshold (7d / 3d / 1d) it builds already_alerted_subq = Notification.user_id WHERE type='plan_ending_soon' AND trigger_type=alert_type (e.g. 'plan_ending_7d'), then filters ~FitnessPlan.user_id.in_(...that...). That subquery has NO created_at filter and NO plan_id scope — it matches EVERY such notification the user has EVER received. create_notification (backend.py:1417-1425) persists trigger_type on the Notification row (verified), so once a user got a 'plan_ending_7d' alert for ANY past plan they are permanently excluded from the 7-day alert forever (and likewise 3d/1d).

IMPACT: exactly the cohort the alert exists for — anyone who finished a plan and started another (renewals, plan changes, goal switches) — silently stops getting "ends in a week / 3 days / tomorrow". The nudge-to-queue-the-next-block loop breaks permanently after the first plan.

REPRO: user completes plan A -> receives 7d/3d/1d alerts (3 Notification rows persist with trigger_type plan_ending_7d/3d/1d). User starts plan B with end_date exactly 7 days out. Next day plan_ending_soon runs -> plans query excludes user (in already_alerted for plan_ending_7d) -> NO alert for plan B. Same at the 3d and 1d marks. Note the alert cannot rely on end_date uniqueness to save it: plan B has a different end_date but the SAME user_id + alert_type, which is all the dedup keys on.

FIX: scope the dedup to the CURRENT plan — either store/compare plan_id (meta_data already carries plan_id) so a per-plan alert fires once per plan, or add a recency window (only dedup within the plan's active window / last N days). Files: app/services/notification_jobs.py:228-266.

fix.description: Root cause: calculateBodyFat (Measurements.tsx) used the IMPERIAL Navy constants (86.010/163.205) but was fed cm, inflating men ~+6.5pts and pinning women at the 50% ceiling. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Measurements: the "Estimated Body Fat (Navy Method)" card uses the IMPERIAL (inches) Navy coefficients but is fed CENTIMETRE values, so every estimate is materially wrong.

calculateBodyFat (src/pages/Measurements.tsx:26-50) uses the inches-form constants - male: 86.010*log10(waist-neck) - 70.041*log10(height) + 36.76; female: 163.205*log10(waist+hip-neck) - 97.684*log10(height) - 78.387 - which are only valid when circumferences AND height are in INCHES. But it passes waist/neck/hip = value_cm (measurement logs are canonical cm) and heightCm straight in. Feeding cm into a log10-of-inches formula adds a fixed offset of (86.010-70.041)*log10(2.54)=+6.47 for men and (163.205-97.684)*log10(2.54)=+26.5 for women.

Node-verified (man waist85/neck38/height178 cm; correct Navy ~16.5%): metric form 495/(1.0324-0.19077*log10(w-n)+0.15456*log10(h))-450 fed cm = 16.44%, imperial form fed inches = 16.49% (they AGREE = correct). This code returns 22.96% - +6.5 too high. Woman waist75/neck32/hip100/height165 cm (correct ~30%) returns 56.8% -> clamps to the 50% ceiling, so essentially EVERY female account shows 50.0% regardless of measurements.

The same defective formula is duplicated in onboarding src/components/onboarding/BodyDiagram.tsx:164-186 (its comment claims "Navy formula requires all inputs in one unit" - true, but the constants demand inches, not cm).

Expected: estimate within Navy method +/-3-4%. Actual: men ~+6.5pts high, women pinned at 50%; it also disagrees with the /body-fat-estimator and /body-composition screens for the same person.

Repro: log waist+neck (+hip if female) on /measurements -> the body-fat card shows an inflated %; female accounts show 50.0%.

Fix: either convert cm->inches before the 86.010/163.205 formula, OR switch to the metric 495/(...) form fed cm. Secondary: key the male/female branch off biological_sex ?? gender (physiology) to match BodyComposition.tsx:145 / BodyFatEstimator.tsx:156 / onboarding-calc.ts:67 - Measurements.tsx:194 currently uses identity gender only.

Files: src/pages/Measurements.tsx:26-50 (calculateBodyFat) + :189-201 (bodyFatEstimate memo; gender source :194); src/components/onboarding/BodyDiagram.tsx:164-186.

fix.description: Root cause: navyMethodMale/navyMethodFemale (BodyFatEstimator.tsx) converted the cm inputs to inches (÷2.54) and then applied the METRIC Navy constants (495/1.0324…), under-reporting body fat by ~6.4pts — and handleSave persisted that low body_fat_pct, corrupting downstream Katch-McArdle BMR/TDEE. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Fat Estimator: the Navy-method calculator converts the user cm inputs to INCHES and then applies the METRIC (cm) Navy coefficients, so it UNDER-estimates body fat by ~6.4 points - and this wrong value is SAVED to the profile.

navyMethodMale (src/pages/BodyFatEstimator.tsx:100-105) does waistIn=waistCm/2.54 (neck/height too), then returns 495/(1.0324 - 0.19077*log10(waistIn-neckIn) + 0.15456*log10(heightIn)) - 450. The 495/(1.0324...) form is the METRIC Navy formula - its constants are calibrated for CENTIMETRES. Feeding it inches shifts the result down by a fixed offset.

Node-verified (man waist85/neck38/height178 cm; correct Navy ~16.5% - confirmed because metric-form-fed-cm 16.44% and imperial-form-fed-inches 16.49% agree): this function returns 10.08%, ~6.4 points too LOW. navyMethodFemale (:107-113) has the identical cm->inches conversion before the metric female constants (1.29579/0.35004/0.22100) - same error.

Worse than a display glitch: handleSave (:289-302) calls healthService.saveBodyFatEstimate(displayedBf) with this under-reported %, persisting body_fat_pct to the profile - which Katch-McArdle BMR keys off (LBM = weight*(1-BF/100)), inflating lean mass and BMR/TDEE downstream.

This is the OPPOSITE-direction sibling of the /measurements Navy bug (that one feeds cm to the imperial form -> +6.5 too high; see companion issue).

Repro: /body-fat-estimator -> Calculator -> Navy tab -> neck 38, waist 85 (cm) -> Calculate -> shows ~10% for a man whose real Navy BF is ~16.5%; Save persists the low value.

Fix: drop the /2.54 conversions and feed cm straight into the 495/(...) metric form (or keep inches but switch to the imperial 86.010/163.205 constants).

Files: src/pages/BodyFatEstimator.tsx:100-113 (navyMethodMale/navyMethodFemale); saved via :293 handleSave.

[suggestion] Vitals logging (fasting blood glucose + blood pressure) on the Measurements screen, condition-gated to users who flagged Diabetes/BP at onboarding.

PROBLEM: Onboarding already asks whether the user has Diabetes or Blood Pressure (Screen5_Health MEDICAL_CONDITIONS), but the app then gives those users nowhere to track those numbers. A diabetic/hypertensive user can log weight and waist, not the two readings their doctor actually cares about, and there is zero feedback loop between their NYUS diet plan and their glucose/BP.

EVIDENCE: India is the diabetes/hypertension capital (~100M+ diabetics, very high BP prevalence) and NYUS is India-focused. Every major India/global tracker (HealthifyMe, MyFitnessPal, Fitbit) logs vitals. We already capture the condition flags at onboarding and do nothing with them beyond content gating. The /measurements page already has the measurement-type + trend-chart infra (waist/neck/hip charts render there via MeasurementChangeChart), so the surface exists.

V1 SCOPE: On /measurements, show a Vitals section ONLY for users who flagged Diabetes and/or BP at onboarding (keeps it out of everyone else's way - calm design). Two manual inputs: fasting blood glucose (mg/dL) and blood pressure (systolic/diastolic), each with a simple trend line reusing MeasurementChangeChart. Manual entry only, no device sync. Tracking-only framing (not diagnosis). Backend: add the vitals measurement types (BP is a two-value pair - the one small schema wrinkle) and reuse the existing measurement POST/GET.

EFFORT: ~1-2 days. FE reuses the Measurements page + chart infra; BE adds measurement types (BP two-value shape is the only wrinkle).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Onboarding Body-Fat % estimator keys off IDENTITY gender, not PHYSIOLOGICAL biological_sex — wrong body-fat reference ladder + wrong metabolic default (a v5 sex/identity-split regression, same class as QA i-20260627-gsex which fixed BMR).

WHERE: Body sub-step of the condensed "You & Goal" step (Screen3_BodyStats). This screen collects biological_sex (Male/Female, REQUIRED — Continue is gated on it) precisely BECAUSE gender is an identity field that can be "Other" and must never drive physiology. But the Body Fat % card on the SAME screen still reads data.gender in 4 spots:
  - reference-guide set:  BODY_FAT_REFERENCES[data.gender === "female" ? "female" : "male"]  (Screen3_BodyStats.tsx:394)
  - un-skip default:      body_fat_pct: data.gender === "female" ? 28 : 20                    (line 333)
  - slider default:       data.body_fat_pct ?? (data.gender === "female" ? 28 : 20)           (line 371)
  - slider clamp default: clampNum(v, 5, 50, data.gender === "female" ? 28 : 20)              (line 373)

REPRO:
  1. Basics tab → Gender = "Other" (a valid identity option, Screen2_BasicInfo.tsx:123).
  2. Body tab → Sex = "Female".
  3. Body Fat % guide shows the MALE ladder (~10/15/20/25/30%) and the default estimate is 20% — directly contradicting the Female sex picked one card above. (Also triggers for Gender="Male" + Sex="Female".)

EXPECTED vs ACTUAL: any user whose biological_sex="female" but gender!="female" (i.e. "male" or "other") should see the FEMALE ladder (~18/22/28/33/38%) and a 28% default; instead they get the MALE ladder + 20% default.

IMPACT: body_fat_pct feeds the metabolism-formula selection (card copy: "helps us choose the most accurate formula for your metabolism") and is persisted + shipped to the backend (sanitizeOnboarding keeps it — OnboardingFlow.tsx:625). So the ~28-vs-20 skew rides through into the plan calc — exactly the BMR-class error the v5 split was built to eliminate.

FIX: swap the 4 `data.gender === "female"` checks to `data.biological_sex === "female"`. biological_sex is guaranteed set on this screen (Continue is gated on it), and the convention already exists in calcOnboardingStats (onboarding-calc.ts uses `data.biological_sex ?? data.gender`). Found by the onboarding-intake bug-hunt (static read; verified against sibling calc convention).

fix.description: Root cause: Dashboard.tsx passed useDashboardData's computed progress (0 when target===0) to useDashboardMoment, so non-training weekdays and plan-less users read as progress 0 and satisfied the *_BEHIND branches, firing the 'your plan is waiting' nag that contradicts the same-screen 'no workout today'/'Generate plan' card. Fix: pass the -1 'no plan/nothing scheduled today' sentinel (gated on dietHasPlan/activityHasPlan target>0) instead of 0, so the sentinel distinguishes 'behind' from 'nothing scheduled'. Proof: regression test test/hooks-useDashboardMoment.test.ts locks the contract both ways (0->BEHIND, -1->generic). The exact rest-day state is not stageable on a single headless capture; the shot shows the healthy dashboard where 'No diet plan yet' now keeps the diet half silent.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Dashboard coach-moment deck nags “Your workout is still doable today — your plan is waiting, tap Activity to begin” on rest / non-training days AND for users with no workout plan, directly contradicting the same-screen activity card that says “no workout today” (or shows the “Generate workout plan” CTA). EXPECTED: on a day with no scheduled workout (or no plan), the coach tip is neutral/rest-oriented, never “you are behind, your plan is waiting.” ACTUAL: the ACTIVITY_BEHIND pool fires. ROOT CAUSE: useDashboardMoment (src/hooks/useMoments.ts:137-143) branches on `activityProgress >= 0 && activityProgress < 20` (ACTIVITY_BEHIND) and `dietProgress >= 0 && dietProgress < 40` (DIET_BEHIND). The `-1` sentinel defaults (lines 119-120) are meant to signal “no plan / unknown → skip these branches,” but Dashboard.tsx (line 196-208) passes the COMPUTED progress from useDashboardData.progressData, which returns a real `0` whenever target is 0 (useDashboardData.ts:151-153: `activityTarget <= 0 ? 0`). target is 0 on any non-training weekday (has_active_plan=true, no session today, is_break_today=false — the exact state DashboardActivityCard.tsx:96 renders “no workout today” for) and for users with no workout plan. So activityProgress===0 satisfies `>=0 && <20` and ACTIVITY_BEHIND is chosen. Verified with a node repro of the branch: passing 0 → ACTIVITY_BEHIND; passing the intended -1 → COACH_GENERIC (correct). REPRO: (1) log in as a user with an active workout plan; open /dashboard on a non-training weekday — activity card shows “no workout today”. (2) scroll to the coach-moment deck (Section 3). (3) tip reads “Your workout is still doable today. … Your plan is waiting — tap Activity to begin.” Same class hits diet (DIET_BEHIND “Protein is still catchable…”) for a user with no diet plan (dietTarget 0 → dietProgress 0). FIX: in Dashboard.tsx pass -1 (or a hasPlan flag) instead of the computed 0 when target===0, or gate the *_BEHIND branches on target>0 (plan exists + session scheduled today) so the sentinel actually distinguishes “behind” from “nothing scheduled.”

fix.description: Root cause: StackedMomentCards.tsx reset expansion via useLayoutEffect keyed on [moments], but Dashboard rebuilds the moments array (new identity) every commit, so the effect re-ran after EVERY parent render (CSAT timer, useCoachMoment async setState, react-query refetch, pull-to-refresh) and snapped any expanded coach tip back to line-clamp-2. Fix: key the reset effect on the content (joined sectionIds) instead of array identity, so expansion resets only when the actual moment set changes. Proof: regression test test/StackedMomentCards.expand.test.tsx proves expansion survives an identical-content array rebuild and still resets when the set changes. This is a pure render-timing bug with no static visual signature; the shot confirms the dashboard/coach deck renders cleanly.

judge.note: Precise root cause, minimal one-line dependency-key fix, regression test covers persist + reset, tsc clean.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Dashboard coach-tip “Tap to read more” expansion collapses itself on any dashboard re-render, so long coach tips cannot be read expanded. ROOT CAUSE: StackedMomentCards.tsx:43-45 runs `useLayoutEffect(() => setExpanded(false), [moments])` to reset expansion when the moment set changes. But the `moments` prop is a BRAND-NEW array on every Dashboard render — Dashboard.tsx:397-435 rebuilds `const items: MomentItem[] = []` inside an inline IIFE each render and passes it straight to <StackedMomentCards moments={items}>. So the `[moments]` dependency changes every commit, the effect runs after EVERY parent render (not only when content changes), and `setExpanded(false)` fires each time. Any Dashboard re-render — the CSAT 4s timer (Dashboard.tsx:162-169), useCoachMoment’s async liveData setState (useMoments.ts:184-195), a react-query background refetch, or pull-to-refresh (handleRefresh) — snaps an expanded tip back to collapsed (line-clamp-2). EXPECTED: once the user taps “Tap to read more,” the tip stays expanded until they collapse it. ACTUAL: it re-collapses on the next parent re-render. REPRO: (1) open /dashboard where the top coach tip is long enough to clamp (shows “Tap to read more” at StackedMomentCards.tsx:144-148). (2) tap the tip to expand. (3) pull-to-refresh (or just wait for a background query refetch / the CSAT timer). → the tip collapses back on its own. FIX: reset expansion only when the moment set actually changes (e.g. key the effect on the joined sectionIds string, not the array identity), or useMemo the `items` array in Dashboard so `moments` is referentially stable across renders.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] After the socket's 'Authentication failed.' recovery reconnect, an OPEN coach-chat screen goes permanently deaf: incoming AI replies never render (while the unread badge lights up), the typing indicator freezes, and the polling fallback never engages. Chain: handleSocketError (chat.service.ts:361) on 'Authentication failed.' refreshes the token, then calls this.disconnect() + this.connect(userId). disconnect() (1) nulls the single-slot callbacks newMessageCallback / aiTypingCallback / errorCallback (chat.service.ts:256-258), which are only registered by useChatSocket's mount effect - a service-internal reconnect re-runs no React effect, so they stay null; and (2) detaches the socket 'disconnect' handler BEFORE calling socket.disconnect() (line 242 vs 254), so disconnectCallbacks never fire, useChatSocket's isSocketConnected stays true, and CoachChat's 60s polling fallback (CoachChat.tsx:104-108) never turns on. Ironically the comment at chat.service.ts:259-265 preserves the connect/disconnect REGISTRIES for exactly this code path but misses the single-slot callbacks two lines above it. Trigger is real: access-token rotation/expiry mid-session or a token_version bump (owner login) makes the backend reject the socket handshake with 'Authentication failed.'; the refresh then succeeds and the recovery path runs. Fix: snapshot + restore the callback slots across the auth-recovery reconnect (or convert them to multi-subscriber registries like connectCallbacks), and invoke disconnectCallbacks on teardown. issues.description: [bug-hunt] Language choice from the startup picker is DESTROYED on every app restart - app always reverts to English. Root cause: main.tsx calls initI18n() with no arg, and config.ts defaults lng=DEFAULT_LOCALE(en), passing an explicit lng:'en' to i18next.init(). Per i18next semantics, an explicit lng bypasses LanguageDetector entirely (stored nyus_locale is never read), AND because detection.caches=['localStorage'], the boot-time changeLanguage('en') REWRITES nyus_locale back to 'en', permanently erasing the user's Hindi/Hinglish choice. Reproduced empirically with the repo's i18next 23.16.8: localStorage nyus_locale='hi' + init with lng:'en' -> language=en and nyus_locale overwritten to 'en'; same init WITHOUT lng -> language=hi, storage intact. Expected: pick Hindi once, app stays Hindi forever. Actual: Hindi only until next launch; picker never re-shows (nyus_lang_picker_shown), so user is stuck in English. Fix: drop the lng option from init (let detector resolve), or pass getStoredLocale() ?? undefined. Files: src/main.tsx:21, src/i18n/config.ts:66-76 (lng param + supportedLngs), src/pages/LanguagePicker.tsx:11-14. Introduced 5f79d6b2 (i18n P1).

[bug-hunt] Activity: completed BODYWEIGHT-only workouts are invisible to the weekly consistency + volume surfaces.

The "Workout sessions this week" weekday dots (TodaysActivityCard) and the Exercise Volume chart both mark a day active only when daily_volume_history[].volume > 0.
